mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 20-day returns in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0% and the annualized GDP growth (computed from GDPC1) exceeds 2.0%, the economy is in a late-cycle expansion phase that leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND GDPC1 annualized growth rate > 2.0%
failure_condition: The Rank IC between the trigger condition and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 60-day returns in periods meeting the trigger condition are not significantly higher than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In the regime of late-cycle expansion (defined by housing starts (HOUST) above 1200 and unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5%), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between the trigger condition and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 20-day returns in periods meeting the trigger condition are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO below 95.0) signals an economic slowdown that increases risk aversion and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between INDPRO and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 60-day returns in periods where INDPRO < 95.0 are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with more negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as elevated labor market slack signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings potential.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between UNRATE and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between UNRATE and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals elevated inflation, which erodes corporate profit margins and increases the risk of monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) are both rising, it signals an inflationary pressure that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between the interaction of CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 60-day returns in periods where both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS are rising are not significantly lower than the baseline (t-test p>0.05).
